'''Nnadubem Gabriel Enyinaya Muoneke''' {{Audio|Ig-Gabe Muoneke.ogg|Listen|help=no}} (born 7 February 1978, in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]) is a Nigerian American retired professional [[basketball]] player and businessman. Despite being born in the United States, Muoneke represented [[Nigeria national basketball team|Nigeria]] internationally.

Muoneke attended [[Cypress Falls High School]] in northwest [[Houston]], [[Texas]]. He then played for four years for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. Undrafted out of college in the NBA, he was a first round pick of the Columbus Riverdragons (now [[Austin Spurs]]) then the [[Roanoke Dazzle]] also of the [[NBDL]]. He has played in multiple [[NBA Summer League|NBA Summer Leagues]] including that of the [[Vancouver Grizzlies]] and the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. Muoneke also signed non-guaranteed NBA contracts with the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Houston Rockets]], [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] and the [[Utah Jazz]] but was waived from all four teams. He has played around the world, including with the [[Ponce Lions (basketball)|Ponce Lions]] in [[Puerto Rico]], [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] in Turkey, the [[Beijing Olympians]] in China, [[Busan KTF Magic Wings]] and [[Seoul SK Knights]] in [[South Korea]], among other places.

== Early life ==
Muoneke was born in 1978 in Michigan to [[Igbo people|Igbo]] Nigerian parents Nik, a math professor, and Njudeka, a medical technologist.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Gabe Muoneke - Hildebrand Department of Petroleum and Geosystems Engineering {{!}} The University of Texas at Austin |url=https://www.pge.utexas.edu/alumnus/gabe-muoneke/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.pge.utexas.edu |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Joaquin M. |author-link=Joaquin Henson |date=October 19, 2008 |title=Another ex-import in NBA roster |url=https://qa.philstar.com/sports/2008/10/19/408340/another-ex-import-nba-roster |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Philstar.com}}</ref> He first studied at St. Christopher’s Private Catholic School as he grew up in [[Houston]], learning Latin, French, and German. He also learned how to play the piano and the saxophone at a young age.<ref name=":1" /> 

When he was 13, Muoneke began pursuing basketball after his father (who at the time was completing his PhD at the [[University of Houston]]) introduced him to [[Hakeem Olajuwon]].<ref name=":1" />

== High school and college career ==
Muoneke attended [[Cypress Falls High School]] in northwest [[Houston]], [[Texas]]. He graduated with a 5.9 GPA and became one of the most sought after high school seniors in the state of Texas and the US.<ref name=":1" />

After graduation, he enrolled at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] on an athletic scholarship.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last= |date=2017-12-03 |title=Living the Dream |url=https://magazine.engr.utexas.edu/2017/living-the-dream |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Texas Engineer |language=en-US}}</ref>

After his sophomore season, he and three other players considered transferring, as "they had lost faith in Penders and his program." [[Tom Penders]] resigned and [[Rick Barnes]] was hired.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 13, 1998 |title=Rick Barnes Leaves Clemson for Texas |url=http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=205506309 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518072338/http://www.clemsontigers.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=28500&ATCLID=205506309 |archive-date=2015-05-18 |access-date=2026-03-31 |work=ClemsonTigers.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=June 19, 1998 |title=PLUS: COLLEGE BASKETBALL -- GEORGE WASHINGTON; Penders Hired |url=http://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/19/sports/plus-college-basketball-george-washington-penders-hired.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518232557/http://www.nytimes.com/1998/06/19/sports/plus-college-basketball-george-washington-penders-hired.html |archive-date=2015-05-18 |access-date=2026-03-31 |language=en}}</ref>

In his junior year, Muoneke led the team in scoring averaging 16.7 points to go with his 6.3 rebounds. In a game against [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]], he punched guard Hennessy Auriantal in the stomach. A month later, against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], he punched [[Nick Bradford]] in the first half and T.J. Pugh twice in the second half. These incidents led to Barnes suspending him for one game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1999-01-20 |title=UT's Gabe Muoneke suspended for punching |url=https://www.oudaily.com/uts-gabe-muoneke-suspended-for-punching/article_48befc2f-6f0d-5cc5-b3fb-c3a12318d4a6.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=OU Daily |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Joaquin M. |author-link=Joaquin Henson |date=June 16, 2002 |title=PBA back in business |url=https://www.philstar.com/sports/2002/06/16/164806/pba-back-business |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Philstar.com}}</ref> Their season ended in the first round of the [[1999 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|Division I tournament]], against 10th seeded [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]], with [[Brian Cardinal]] stealing his inbounds pass in the final seconds to seal the win.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1999-03-11 |title=No. 10 Purdue Sails By Texas - CBS News |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/no-10-purdue-sails-by-texas/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In his final year, Muoneke averaged 13.7 points and 6.3 rebounds.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |date=2003-02-04 |title=Gabe Muoneke está al caer |url=https://www.elperiodicoextremadura.com/deportes/2003/02/04/gabe-muoneke-caer-45764412.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=El Periódico Extremadura |language=es}}</ref> He graduated in 2002 with his degree in Petroleum Engineering. He finished his college career ranked in the top 15 in the history of University of Texas basketball in scoring (1,456 points),<ref>{{Cite news |last=Novak |first=Thad |date=June 7, 2018 |title=Texas Basketball: The Top 50 Players in School History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1167696-texas-basketball-the-top-50-players-in-school-history |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250811015230/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1167696-texas-basketball-the-top-50-players-in-school-history |archive-date=2025-08-11 |access-date=2026-03-31 |language=en}}</ref> rebounding, and top 20 in games played and started.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":1" />

== Professional career ==

=== Fort Wayne Fury ===
Muoneke applied for the [[2000 NBA draft|2000 NBA Draft]], where he went undrafted.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA DRAFT 2000: Position F |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft00/positions/position3.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref> He was then drafted in the sixth round of the 2000 [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]] draft by the [[Fort Wayne Fury]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ESPN.com: CBA - 2000 CBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/cba/news/2000/0920/759513.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

=== Boca Juniors ===
Muoneke then spent some time overseas, averaging 19 points and 9.5 rebounds in Turkey ([[Pinar Karsiyaka]]).<ref name=":7" /> He then averaged and 19.8 points and 4.7 rebounds in Argentina with the [[Boca Juniors (basketball)|Boca Juniors]] and contributed to their playoff run.<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2001-04-21 |title=Boca sacó diferencias en el comienzo de la serie |url=https://www.lanacion.com.ar/deportes/boca-saco-diferencias-en-el-comienzo-de-la-serie-nid60789/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=LA NACION |language=es}}</ref> 

=== Columbus Riverdragons ===
Muoneke then returned to the US, where he became a first round pick (fourth overall) of the Columbus Riverdragons (now [[Austin Spurs]]) in the inaugural [[NBDL]] draft in [[2001 National Basketball Development League draft|2001]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 D-League Draft |url=https://nbahoopsonline.com/History/Leagues/NBDL/Draft.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=nbahoopsonline.com}}</ref> He scored 33 points against the [[North Charleston Lowgators]] on 7 February, 2002.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=100 point scorers |url=http://www.luckyshow.org/basketball/100pts.htm |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.luckyshow.org}}</ref> In his time with them, he averaged 17.1 points and 5.9 rebounds.<ref name=":7" />

=== Purefoods TJ Hotdogs ===
In 2002, Muoneke came to the Philippines to play for a [[Champions for Christ]] team. He decided to stay in the country, which led to him becoming an import for the [[Purefoods TJ Hotdogs]] for that year's [[2002 PBA Commissioner's Cup|PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref name=":6" /> Playing alongside another import in Kelvin Price, they were replaced midway through the elimination round by Warren Rosegreen and former NBA veteran [[Chris Morris (basketball)|Chris Morris]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sulit |first=Jutt |date=2020-07-30 |title=Notable NBA players who played in the PBA |url=https://www.espn.ph/basketball/story/_/id/29550566/notable-nba-players-played-pba |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In six games with Purefoods, he averaged 28 points.<ref name=":2" />

=== Roanoke Dazzle ===
On 1 October 2002, Muoneke was signed by the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2002-10-01 |title=Transactions |url=https://www.deseret.com/2002/10/1/19680484/transactions/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Deseret News |language=en}}</ref> On 25 October, he and [[Ricky Moore (basketball)|Ricky Moore]] were waived.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 26, 2002 |title=NBA Transactions |url=https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=ade20021026-01.1.10&e=-------en-20--1--txt-txIN---------- |access-date=March 31, 2026 |work=[[Adirondack Daily Enterprise]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Joaquin M. |author-link=Joaquin Henson |date=November 1, 2002 |title=7 ex-imports survive NBA cut |url=https://www.philstar.com/sports/2002/11/01/182198/7-ex-imports-survive-nba-cut |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Philstar.com}}</ref>

On 18 January 2003, he scored 38 points against the [[Fayetteville Patriots]].<ref name=":4" /> He was averaging 22.1 points and 8.8 rebounds in the NBDL with the [[Roanoke Dazzle]] before he left the team to play in Spain.<ref name=":7" />

=== CB Cáceres ===
On 4 February 2003, [[CB Cáceres]] of the Spanish league [[LEB Oro]] finalized Muoneke's release from the Roanoke Dazzle and signed him as a replacement for [[Deon Thomas]].<ref name=":7" />

=== Saba Battery ===
In March 2007, Muoneke played for [[Saba Battery Tehran BC|Saba Battery]] in Iran, helping them win the [[2007 FIBA Asia Champions Cup]].<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |last=GONZÁLEZ |first=D. |date=2007-12-26 |title=El Baskonia ultima el fichaje del ala-pívot Muoneke |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/alava/20071226/deportes/tau/baskonia-ultima-fichaje-pivot-20071226.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=El Correo |language=es}}</ref>

=== Rio Grande Valley Vipers ===
In his time with the team, Muoneke averaged 26.2 points and 5.3 rebounds.<ref name=":9">{{Cite web |last=DIGITAL |first=EL CORREO |date=2007-12-27 |title=Muoneke firma por tres meses con el TAU y se incorpora a la expedición baskonista que viaja a Sevilla |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/alava/20071227/deportes/tau/muoneke-firma-tres-meses-200712271350.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=El Correo |language=es}}</ref>

=== TAU Cerámica ===
On 26 December, 2007, Muoneke signed a three-month deal with [[Saski Baskonia|TAU Cerámica]] of the [[Liga ACB]] to replace the injured [[James Singleton (basketball)|James Singleton]].<ref name=":9" /><ref name=":8" /> When the contract expired, the team's renewal offer was not accepted by Muoneke and both parties mutually parted ways.

=== ASVEL Villeurbanne ===
After another stint with Saba Battery, in August of 2008, Muoneke signed with [[ASVEL Villeurbanne]] in France for the [[2008–09 Pro A season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=PPLL |date=2008-08-13 |title=El nigeriano recala en el Asvel francés |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/vizcaya/20080813/deportes/mas-baloncesto/nigeriano-recala-asvel-frances-20080813.html |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=El Correo |language=es}}</ref> He did not stay long with the team, as he was released in September. He then signed with the [[Utah Jazz]] but was waived in October.

=== Yunnan Running Bulls ===
During his time in China, Muoneke broke many scoring records and was amongst the top scorers in China in all three of his seasons in the country. While playing for the [[Yunnan Running Bulls]], Muoneke was physically attacked during a postgame confrontation between himself and Chinese national team captain and [[Shanghai Sharks]] player [[Liu Wei (basketball)|Liu Wei]]. After Muoneke and the Sharks' Cai Liang wrestled for the ball during the game, Cai, Liu and some Sharks players confronted Muoneke, his wife, children and mother-in-law as they were leaving the stadium. Muoneke had a water bottle thrown at him, before being chased and cornered by the players. Liu and Cai were subsequently fined and suspended. The Shanghai Sharks were also fined. Muoneke was not injured.<ref>{{Cite news |title=China captain punished for postgame clash |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3746883 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250602001521/https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3746883 |archive-date=2025-06-02 |access-date=2026-03-31 |work=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On his blog in 2009, he alluded to a retirement from professional basketball and subsequently did retire in 2010 at the age of 30.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://blogs.hoopshype.com/blogs/muoneke/index.php |title=HoopsHype.com NBA Blogs - Gabe Muoneke |access-date=17 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080303185223/http://blogs.hoopshype.com/blogs/muoneke/index.php |archive-date=3 March 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-03-01 |title=Zoco europeo: Gabe Muoneke se retira y Baston se va a Ucrania |url=https://www.solobasket.com/liga-endesa/zoco-europeo-gabe-muoneke-se-retira-y-baston-se-va-ucrania |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Últimas Noticias de baloncesto {{!}} Solobasket |language=es}}</ref>

== National team career ==
Muoneke was first called up to the [[Nigeria men's national basketball team]] in 2003 for the [[2003 FIBA Africa Championship]], where they finished second. He then played in the [[2005 FIBA Africa Championship]] and the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]]. He was then named captain for the team competing in the [[2009 FIBA Africa Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-08-13 |title=NGR - Muoneke leading the Nigeria quest |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/ngr-muoneke-leading-the-nigeria-quest |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

== Post-playing career ==
As he was playing overseas, Muoneke lay the groundwork for his energy industry plans by building connections with financiers and influencers. When he retired in 2009, he focused on his career in African oil and gas. He first joined [[Afren]], a U.K.-based oil exploration and production company.<ref name=":3" /> He then started MTX, a Nigerian-based energy company.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />

== Personal life ==
Muoneke has been married to Lenea Muoneke. They have four children, Muo, Bianna, Arianna, and Zibem.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bianna Muoneke - 2026 - Volleyball |url=https://georgiadogs.com/sports/womens-volleyball/roster/bianna-muoneke/10480 |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=University of Georgia Athletics |language=en}}</ref> Their son Muo played basketball for the [[Abilene Christian Wildcats men's basketball|Abilene Christian Wildcats]] while Bianna and Arianna played volleyball for the [[Georgia Bulldogs women's volleyball|Georgia Bulldogs]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-16 |title=Muodubem Muoneke - Men's Basketball |url=https://acusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/muodubem-muoneke/9834 |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Abilene Christian Athletics |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bulldogs Ink Four for 2026 Season |url=https://georgiadogs.com/news/2025/11/12/georgia-volleyball-signing-day-central |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=University of Georgia Athletics |language=en}}</ref> 

Muoneke is a [[born-again Christian]]. He received counseling for his outbursts in college which led to him embracing Christianity. His name Nnadubem means "God guide me".<ref name=":6" />

Beginning in November 2007, Muoneke had been maintaining a blog on [[HoopsHype.com|Hoopshype.com]], where he discusses his playing career, life in foreign countries, and politics.<ref name=":0" /> His final blog post was published in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HoopsHype.com NBA Blogs - Gabe Muoneke » The final blog |url=http://blogs.hoopshype.com/blogs/muoneke/2011/02/16/the-final-blog/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110220223216/http://blogs.hoopshype.com/blogs/muoneke/2011/02/16/the-final-blog/ |archive-date=2011-02-20 |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=blogs.hoopshype.com}}</ref> He is capable of speaking seven languages, including Hebrew, and is also a [[Brazilian jiu-jitsu]] [[Brown belt (Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu)|brown belt]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" /> 

In 2013, Muoneke was arrested at [[George Bush Intercontinental Airport]] for bringing a knife. After 30 hours in two different jails, he was released on bail.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=2013-06-05 |title=Former basketball player says he had no idea knife was in carry-on bag |url=https://www.khou.com/article/news/local/former-basketball-player-says-he-had-no-idea-knife-was-in-carry-on-bag/285-320972902 |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=khou.com |language=en-US}}</ref> The case was dismissed on 4 June of that year, as he had accidentally brought a kitchen knife, which he used to use for carving mangoes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christian |first=Carol |date=2013-06-05 |title=Ex-UT player with knife at Bush airport has charges dropped |url=https://www.chron.com/news/houston-texas/houston/article/ex-ut-player-with-knife-at-bush-airport-has-4580516.php |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Chron |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":5" />
